newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress asked to withdraw leadership bid.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress asked to withdraw leadership bid.

text.p: India's ousted United Front coalition on Thursday asked the Congress party to withdraw its official bid to form a new government ahead of a coalition agreement on a new prime minister.
Congress president Sitaram Kesri wrote to President Shankar Dayal Sharma on March 31 formally staking the party's claim to head a new government.

"The letter is proving to be a stumbling block," a senior United Front official told reporters. "The Left parties (in the coalition) have already asked the Congress to withdraw it. The other constituents also appreciate the Left stand and recognise the need for it."

The official's comments followed several meetings between United Front Convener Chandrababu Naidu and Kesri to end the uncertainty triggered by the fall of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government in a vote of confidence on April 11.
"There are problems which need to be sorted out," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters earlier on Thursday. "I am confident that all problems will be resolved."
Reddy said the 15-party coalition's decision-making Steering Committee would meet at 9.30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday to elect a new leader to replace Deve Gowda, ending a 19-day political crisis.
The Press Trust of India said Kesri held informal consultations with the decision-making Congress Working Committee on Thursday to resolve the political impasse.
The 15-party alliance postponed a decision on who would replace Deve Gowda due to political infighting and the death of a veteran party boss, coalition leaders said.
Deve Gowda also attended the steering committee meeting on Thursday.

His downfall was precipitated by the Congress party, which had shored up the minority coalition for 10 months but abruptly withdrew its backing on March 30, accusing the alliance of trying to sideline India's oldest party.
But the United Front and Congress, fearing a return to power by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), have since agreed to try to patch up their differences.
Congress said on Monday it would support a new government led by the same alliance, provided the United Front replaced Deve Gowda.
Congress has said withdrawal of its official letter to the president would be a formality once the United Front selected a new chief.
But the four left-wing parties in the alliance, including India's two main communist groups, said on Wednesday they would insist that Congress move first.
The Left Front fears Congress could make an eventual push for power.

The United Front's Steering Committee met on Thursday afternoon but quickly adjourned after paying its respects to veteran politician Biju Patnaik, who died earlier in the day in a New Delhi hospital.
Patnaik was a former chief minister of the eastern Indian state of Orissa.
